sections.title: 145-Question Full Practice Examination
sections.html:
145-Question Full Practice Examination

Simulation rules Set a 150-minute timer. Use no notes. Answer every question. Flag uncertain items and return only after completing the first pass. The mix is 110 general-style and 35 Texas-style questions, matching the scored-plus-pretest presentation in the current outline.

These are original study questions, not Pearson VUE exam questions. Their purpose is to test the official content categories and vocabulary under realistic time pressure.

1. Sunday is reviewing Rideshare/TNC exposure. Which explanation is correct?

A. Residential property insurer of last resort offering basic coverage when eligible applicants cannot obtain coverage in the voluntary admitted market; TDI guidance says at least two companies must decline.

B. Generally within 15 calendar days after notice of a first-party claim, the insurer acknowledges, begins investigation, and requests needed items.

C. Coverage needs change when the app is off, on and waiting, and carrying or traveling to a passenger. Personal policies may exclude commercial/livery activity.

D. Current TDI consumer guidance states the company must give 10 days' notice before cancellation, subject to the policy and law.

2. On the Texas P&C exam, Symbol 2 - Owned autos only is best understood as:

A. Vacant generally means substantially empty of people and contents needed for use; unoccupied means furnished but no one is present.

B. Restoring the insured approximately to the financial position held before the loss - not allowing profit from insurance.

C. Basic and Broad list named causes; Special covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.

D. Covers autos the insured owns, subject to the coverage shown.

3. Choose the most accurate statement about Combined single limit.

A. Covers customers' autos in the insured's care, custody, or control for servicing, repair, parking, or similar operations.

B. The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

C. Additional time to report claims after claims-made coverage ends; it does not extend the policy period or cover new acts.

D. One liability limit applies to bodily injury and property damage together per accident.

4. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Stock insurer?

A. Owned by stockholders.

B. Texas-specific statutory concept referenced in the exam outline for certain fire-loss claims; learn the outline reference, TIC Section 862.053, and read the question's facts carefully.

C. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

D. Lifetime income benefits apply to specifically defined catastrophic injuries.

5. Which statement best describes Products-completed operations?

A. Causes, property, persons, or situations the policy does not cover.

B. Replace a portion of wages when a compensable injury reduces earning ability, subject to law.

C. Condominium unit-owner coverage for personal property, certain building items, loss assessments, liability, and additional living expense.

D. Liability after a product leaves the insured's control or work is completed away from the insured's premises.

6. Sunday is reviewing Commercial property form. Which explanation is correct?

A. Uncertainty about loss. Insurance is designed mainly for pure risk, where loss or no loss - but not gain - is possible.

B. A lawful financial relationship in which the insured would suffer loss if the property is damaged or the liability occurs.

C. Can cover buildings, business personal property, and personal property of others within described rules and limits.

D. Begins after the covered direct loss subject to the form and ends when property should be repaired/rebuilt or operations resume at a new location, as defined.

7. On the Texas P&C exam, Guaranty association is best understood as:

A. Current TDI consumer guidance states the company must give 10 days' notice before cancellation, subject to the policy and law.

B. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

C. An employer that does not provide Texas statutory workers compensation and must meet notice/reporting requirements.

D. Organized under another U.S. state or jurisdiction.

8. Choose the most accurate statement about ACV formula.

A. Limited reimbursement for temporary transportation after a covered physical-damage loss, subject to form triggers and limits.

B. Uncertainty about loss. Insurance is designed mainly for pure risk, where loss or no loss - but not gain - is possible.

C. Condominium unit-owner coverage for personal property, certain building items, loss assessments, liability, and additional living expense.

D. Replacement cost - depreciation = actual cash value.

9. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Duty?

A. Statutory benefits for eligible beneficiaries and funeral costs after covered work-related death.

B. Replace a portion of wages when a compensable injury reduces earning ability, subject to law.

C. A lawful financial relationship in which the insured would suffer loss if the property is damaged or the liability occurs.

D. A legal obligation to act or refrain from acting with the required standard of care.

10. Which statement best describes Alien insurer?

A. Owned by policyholders.

B. Organized under the laws of another country.

C. Impairment income benefits are tied to a permanent impairment rating after maximum medical improvement.

D. Included/offered in Texas auto policies at a statutory minimum of $2,500 unless the named insured rejects it in writing; pays covered medical expenses plus qualifying lost income/essential services.

11. Sunday is reviewing Workers comp manual premium. Which explanation is correct?

A. Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

B. Begins after the covered direct loss subject to the form and ends when property should be repaired/rebuilt or operations resume at a new location, as defined.

C. One liability limit applies to bodily injury and property damage together per accident.

D. Examples include theft, fire, vandalism, glass breakage, flood, hail, falling objects, and contact with a bird or animal.

12. On the Texas P&C exam, Other than collision is best understood as:

A. Examples include theft, fire, vandalism, glass breakage, flood, hail, falling objects, and contact with a bird or animal.

B. Only the insurer makes a legally enforceable promise to pay if conditions are met.

C. The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

D. E personal liability; F medical payments to others, generally without requiring proof of negligence.

13. Choose the most accurate statement about Direct loss.

A. Immediate physical damage caused by a covered peril, such as hail damaging a roof.

B. Pays damages for bodily injury or property damage for which an insured becomes legally responsible, plus defense and supplementary payments.

C. Amount carried / amount required x covered loss - deductible, never exceeding applicable limit or loss.

D. Open-peril coverage on dwelling, other structures, and personal property, subject to exclusions.

14. Which answer correctly applies the concept of General compensatory damages?

A. Common exam formula: replacement cost minus depreciation.

B. Provides higher limits and may cover some claims not covered by underlying insurance, subject to retention and terms.

C. Non-economic harm such as pain, suffering, mental anguish, or disfigurement.

D. A vehicle not owned by or furnished/available for the regular use of the named insured or family member.

15. Which statement best describes Basic/Broad/Special causes of loss?

A. Temporary evidence of insurance until the policy is issued or the binder expires.

B. Protects insureds when an at-fault driver has no insurance, insufficient limits, or in covered hit-and-run situations.

C. Open-peril building coverage with named-peril personal-property coverage.

D. Basic and Broad list named causes; Special covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.

16. Sunday is reviewing Contribution. Which explanation is correct?

A. Named-peril coverage for dwelling, other structures, and personal property.

B. Allocation among insurers or responsible parties that share the same loss.

C. Limited reimbursement for temporary transportation after a covered physical-damage loss, subject to form triggers and limits.

D. Renters coverage; primarily personal property, loss of use, liability, and medical payments, not the building.

17. On the Texas P&C exam, Temporary substitute is best understood as:

A. Upset of the covered auto or impact with another vehicle or object.

B. Covers only autos scheduled in the policy for the indicated coverage.

C. A non-owned auto temporarily used because a covered auto is out of normal use due to breakdown, repair, servicing, loss, or destruction.

D. Liability after a product leaves the insured's control or work is completed away from the insured's premises.

18. Choose the most accurate statement about Death and burial benefits.

A. Failure to meet the required standard of care.

B. Restoring the insured approximately to the financial position held before the loss - not allowing profit from insurance.

C. Statutory benefits for eligible beneficiaries and funeral costs after covered work-related death.

D. The insured and insurer agree in advance on the value; a related endorsement may suspend coinsurance.

19. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Conditions?

A. Pays reasonable medical and funeral expenses for covered persons, generally without regard to fault and subject to time/limit provisions.

B. Liability imposed on one party for another's acts because of a legal relationship, such as an employer for an employee acting in scope.

C. Rules and duties governing coverage, such as prompt notice, cooperation, proof of loss, and protecting property.

D. Generally triggered by covered injury or damage occurring during the policy period, even if the claim is made later.

20. Which statement best describes Actual cash value?

A. Pays covered damages for employer liability not handled by workers compensation law, subject to stated limits and exclusions.

B. Common exam formula: replacement cost minus depreciation.

C. Property value x coinsurance percentage.

D. Scheduled inland-marine coverage for high-value movable property, usually broader than homeowners special limits.

21. Sunday is reviewing Claims-made form. Which explanation is correct?

A. Open-peril coverage on dwelling, other structures, and personal property, subject to exclusions.

B. Broader named-peril protection and typically replacement-cost settlement on covered buildings when requirements are met.

C. One limit applies to one described property or location.

D. Generally requires the claim to be first made during the policy period or reporting period and after any applicable retroactive date.

22. On the Texas P&C exam, HO-5 Comprehensive is best understood as:

A. Protects an employer or organization against employee dishonesty; it resembles insurance more than a performance guarantee.

B. Rules and duties governing coverage, such as prompt notice, cooperation, proof of loss, and protecting property.

C. Broad liability designation that can include owned, hired, and non-owned autos when shown.

D. Open-peril coverage on dwelling, other structures, and personal property, subject to exclusions.

23. Choose the most accurate statement about Medical payments.

A. Pays reasonable medical and funeral expenses for covered persons, generally without regard to fault and subject to time/limit provisions.

B. Additional time to report claims after claims-made coverage ends; it does not extend the policy period or cover new acts.

C. Limited medical payments for qualifying injuries, generally without proof of negligence.

D. The insurer drafts the contract; genuine ambiguity is generally construed against the drafter.

24. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Non-owned auto?

A. Words given special policy meanings; defined terms control even if ordinary speech differs.

B. Apply the per-person bodily injury cap, then the per-accident bodily injury cap, then the separate property damage cap.

C. The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

D. A vehicle not owned by or furnished/available for the regular use of the named insured or family member.

25. Which statement best describes Split limits?

A. A listed value that may still be subject to policy settlement terms; it is not automatically a guaranteed payout.

B. Separate per-person bodily injury, per-accident bodily injury, and per-accident property damage limits.

C. Generally requires the claim to be first made during the policy period or reporting period and after any applicable retroactive date.

D. After paying a covered loss, the insurer acquires the insured's right to recover from a responsible third party.

26. Sunday is reviewing Fidelity bond. Which explanation is correct?

A. Uncertainty about loss. Insurance is designed mainly for pure risk, where loss or no loss - but not gain - is possible.

B. Named-peril coverage for dwelling, other structures, and personal property.

C. Protects an employer or organization against employee dishonesty; it resembles insurance more than a performance guarantee.

D. The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

27. On the Texas P&C exam, Prompt acknowledgement is best understood as:

A. When sued, a nonsubscriber generally loses traditional defenses including employee contributory negligence, fellow-servant negligence, and assumption of risk.

B. Coverage needs change when the app is off, on and waiting, and carrying or traveling to a passenger. Personal policies may exclude commercial/livery activity.

C. Organized under another U.S. state or jurisdiction.

D. Generally within 15 calendar days after notice of a first-party claim, the insurer acknowledges, begins investigation, and requests needed items.

28. Choose the most accurate statement about Medical benefits.

A. Allocation among insurers or responsible parties that share the same loss.

B. Reasonable and necessary care for a compensable work injury, as state law provides.

C. One liability limit applies to bodily injury and property damage together per accident.

D. Immediate physical damage caused by a covered peril, such as hail damaging a roof.

29. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Replacement cost?

A. The breach must be both the actual and legally proximate cause of injury.

B. Cost to repair or replace with property of like kind and quality without deduction for depreciation, subject to policy rules.

C. Property value x coinsurance percentage.

D. Covers qualifying loss of net income plus continuing normal operating expenses during the period of restoration after covered direct damage.

30. Which statement best describes Texas private employer rule?

A. Current TDI consumer guidance states the company must give 10 days' notice before cancellation, subject to the policy and law.

B. Most private employers may choose whether to carry workers compensation; private employers on government contracts may be required to cover project workers.

C. An insurer's authorization for an agent to act on its behalf, subject to Texas filing and termination rules.

D. Owned by stockholders.

31. Sunday is reviewing CGL Coverage C. Which explanation is correct?

A. Waiver is voluntary surrender of a known right; estoppel prevents a party from asserting a right after conduct caused reasonable detrimental reliance.

B. The immediate cause of loss, such as fire, wind, theft, collision, or lightning.

C. Covers only causes of loss listed in the policy; the insured generally must show a listed peril caused the loss.

D. Limited medical payments for qualifying injuries, generally without proof of negligence.

32. On the Texas P&C exam, Garagekeepers is best understood as:

A. The insurer's obligation depends on the insured satisfying policy duties and conditions.

B. Liability imposed on one party for another's acts because of a legal relationship, such as an employer for an employee acting in scope.

C. Covers customers' autos in the insured's care, custody, or control for servicing, repair, parking, or similar operations.

D. Can cover buildings, business personal property, and personal property of others within described rules and limits.

33. Choose the most accurate statement about Conditional.

A. Pays covered damages for employer liability not handled by workers compensation law, subject to stated limits and exclusions.

B. Only the insurer makes a legally enforceable promise to pay if conditions are met.

C. The insurer's obligation depends on the insured satisfying policy duties and conditions.

D. Condominium unit-owner coverage for personal property, certain building items, loss assessments, liability, and additional living expense.

34. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Hazard?

A. Separate per-person bodily injury, per-accident bodily injury, and per-accident property damage limits.

B. Only the insurer makes a legally enforceable promise to pay if conditions are met.

C. A condition that increases the chance or severity of loss. Physical hazards are tangible; moral hazards involve dishonesty; morale hazards involve carelessness.

D. Begins after the covered direct loss subject to the form and ends when property should be repaired/rebuilt or operations resume at a new location, as defined.

35. Which statement best describes Theft?

A. A condition that increases the chance or severity of loss. Physical hazards are tangible; moral hazards involve dishonesty; morale hazards involve carelessness.

B. Adds limits above underlying coverage and generally follows the underlying scope more closely.

C. Broad unlawful taking of property.

D. Failure to meet the required standard of care.

36. Sunday is reviewing Personal articles floater. Which explanation is correct?

A. Words such as EXCEPT, NOT, BEST, FIRST, PRIMARY, and MOST LIKELY change the task and should be marked mentally.

B. One liability limit applies to bodily injury and property damage together per accident.

C. Scheduled inland-marine coverage for high-value movable property, usually broader than homeowners special limits.

D. Replace a portion of wages when a compensable injury reduces earning ability, subject to law.

37. On the Texas P&C exam, Surplus lines is best understood as:

A. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

B. Coverage placed with eligible nonadmitted insurers for qualifying risks that cannot be placed in the admitted market, through properly licensed surplus lines channels.

C. Generally within 15 business days after receiving required items, the insurer accepts or rejects; it may extend up to 45 days with notice and reason.

D. A driver must be able to show compliance through an allowed method, most commonly liability insurance meeting minimum limits.

38. Choose the most accurate statement about PIP.

A. Broader no-fault protection than medical payments because it can include lost income and essential services in addition to medical expenses.

B. Covers only causes of loss listed in the policy; the insured generally must show a listed peril caused the loss.

C. After paying a covered loss, the insurer acquires the insured's right to recover from a responsible third party.

D. Liability after a product leaves the insured's control or work is completed away from the insured's premises.

39. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Exclusive remedy?

A. Generally requires the claim to be first made during the policy period or reporting period and after any applicable retroactive date.

B. Protects insureds when an at-fault driver has no insurance, insufficient limits, or in covered hit-and-run situations.

C. Workers compensation benefits generally replace an employee's tort suit against a covered employer for ordinary work injury, subject to exceptions.

D. Adds limits above underlying coverage and generally follows the underlying scope more closely.

40. Which statement best describes Equipment breakdown?

A. The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

B. Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

C. Addresses accidental mechanical/electrical breakdown and related property/business-income consequences that ordinary property forms may exclude.

D. The insurer drafts the contract; genuine ambiguity is generally construed against the drafter.

41. Sunday is reviewing TIBs. Which explanation is correct?

A. Owned by policyholders.

B. Temporary income benefits replace part of lost wages during qualifying temporary disability.

C. Included/offered in Texas auto policies at a statutory minimum of $2,500 unless the named insured rejects it in writing; pays covered medical expenses plus qualifying lost income/essential services.

D. Allows sale of home, auto, commercial, liability, and other property/casualty lines within license authority.

42. On the Texas P&C exam, Blanket insurance is best understood as:

A. Words such as EXCEPT, NOT, BEST, FIRST, PRIMARY, and MOST LIKELY change the task and should be marked mentally.

B. One limit applies across multiple properties, locations, or classes of property.

C. Can cover the insured's own response, restoration, business interruption, notification, and extortion expenses, depending on form.

D. The dominant, efficient cause that sets an unbroken chain of events in motion.

43. Choose the most accurate statement about Representation.

A. Liability without the ordinary need to prove negligence for defined activities or defective products; defenses and statutes still matter.

B. A statement believed true to the best of the applicant's knowledge; a material false statement can affect coverage.

C. An even stronger form of liability imposed by law for certain activities, with very limited defenses.

D. Only the insurer makes a legally enforceable promise to pay if conditions are met.

44. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Coinsurance?

A. Covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited; exclusions become especially important.

B. Requires insurance to a specified percentage of value. Partial-loss payment is generally Did carry / Should have carried x Loss, minus deductible.

C. As the number of similar independent exposure units grows, actual loss experience becomes more predictable.

D. Designed to punish and deter especially wrongful conduct rather than compensate ordinary loss.

45. Which statement best describes Appointment?

A. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

B. An insurer's authorization for an agent to act on its behalf, subject to Texas filing and termination rules.

C. Generally payment is due within 5 business days after the insurer notifies the claimant it will pay, subject to statutory exceptions.

D. An employer that does not provide Texas statutory workers compensation and must meet notice/reporting requirements.

46. Sunday is reviewing Nonsubscriber. Which explanation is correct?

A. An insurer's authorization for an agent to act on its behalf, subject to Texas filing and termination rules.

B. An employer that does not provide Texas statutory workers compensation and must meet notice/reporting requirements.

C. Current TDI guidance generally requires 60 days' notice for policies bought or renewed in 2024 or later; older-transition rules may differ.

D. Generally within 15 business days after receiving required items, the insurer accepts or rejects; it may extend up to 45 days with notice and reason.

47. On the Texas P&C exam, Medical, death, burial is best understood as:

A. Texas Automobile Insurance Plan Association makes required auto liability coverage available to eligible applicants unable to obtain it through the voluntary market.

B. Other major statutory benefit categories for compensable injury or death.

C. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

D. $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 property damage per accident - Texas minimum financial responsibility limits.

48. Choose the most accurate statement about Indirect loss.

A. Immediate physical damage caused by a covered peril, such as hail damaging a roof.

B. Broader named-peril protection and typically replacement-cost settlement on covered buildings when requirements are met.

C. A vehicle not owned by or furnished/available for the regular use of the named insured or family member.

D. A consequence of direct loss, such as lost rent while a damaged house is repaired.

49. Which answer correctly applies the concept of BOP?

A. A lawful financial relationship in which the insured would suffer loss if the property is damaged or the liability occurs.

B. The most the policy pays for specified categories of covered loss during the policy period.

C. A packaged policy for eligible small-to-medium businesses combining property and liability, with standardized coverage and eligibility rules.

D. Pays reasonable medical and funeral expenses for covered persons, generally without regard to fault and subject to time/limit provisions.

50. Which statement best describes DP-2 Broad?

A. Broader named-peril protection and typically replacement-cost settlement on covered buildings when requirements are met.

B. Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

C. A packaged policy for eligible small-to-medium businesses combining property and liability, with standardized coverage and eligibility rules.

D. Separate per-person bodily injury, per-accident bodily injury, and per-accident property damage limits.

51. Sunday is reviewing Strict liability. Which explanation is correct?

A. A modular commercial package built from common declarations/conditions plus selected coverage parts; it is not itself one coverage grant.

B. Liability without the ordinary need to prove negligence for defined activities or defective products; defenses and statutes still matter.

C. Apply the per-person bodily injury cap, then the per-accident bodily injury cap, then the separate property damage cap.

D. Autos not owned, leased, hired, rented, or borrowed by the business but used in its business, often employee-owned vehicles.

52. On the Texas P&C exam, Transportation expense is best understood as:

A. Limited reimbursement for temporary transportation after a covered physical-damage loss, subject to form triggers and limits.

B. Scheduled inland-marine coverage for high-value movable property, usually broader than homeowners special limits.

C. Basic named perils, commonly fire, lightning, and internal explosion; extended coverage and vandalism may be added.

D. Incurred losses divided by earned premium; useful as an underwriting/performance concept.

53. Choose the most accurate statement about Symbol 9 - Non-owned autos.

A. Autos not owned, leased, hired, rented, or borrowed by the business but used in its business, often employee-owned vehicles.

B. Addresses accidental mechanical/electrical breakdown and related property/business-income consequences that ordinary property forms may exclude.

C. Targets employment-related claims such as wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

D. A packaged policy for eligible small-to-medium businesses combining property and liability, with standardized coverage and eligibility rules.

54. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Stated value?

A. Examples include theft, fire, vandalism, glass breakage, flood, hail, falling objects, and contact with a bird or animal.

B. Cuts off coverage for injury-causing acts occurring before the stated date under a claims-made form.

C. Three parties: principal promises performance, obligee receives the promise, and surety guarantees it. The surety expects reimbursement from the principal.

D. A listed value that may still be subject to policy settlement terms; it is not automatically a guaranteed payout.

55. Which statement best describes NFIP?

A. As the number of similar independent exposure units grows, actual loss experience becomes more predictable.

B. Restoring the insured approximately to the financial position held before the loss - not allowing profit from insurance.

C. Federal flood program offering separate building and contents coverage. Standard property and homeowners policies generally exclude flood.

D. Pays reasonable medical and funeral expenses for covered persons, generally without regard to fault and subject to time/limit provisions.

56. Sunday is reviewing Business income. Which explanation is correct?

A. An auto the named insured becomes owner of during the policy period, subject to policy notice and coverage rules.

B. Covers qualifying loss of net income plus continuing normal operating expenses during the period of restoration after covered direct damage.

C. Vacant generally means substantially empty of people and contents needed for use; unoccupied means furnished but no one is present.

D. Broader no-fault protection than medical payments because it can include lost income and essential services in addition to medical expenses.

57. On the Texas P&C exam, Definitions is best understood as:

A. Basic named perils, commonly fire, lightning, and internal explosion; extended coverage and vandalism may be added.

B. Replacement cost - depreciation = actual cash value.

C. Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

D. Words given special policy meanings; defined terms control even if ordinary speech differs.

58. Choose the most accurate statement about Employee dishonesty.

A. Words given special policy meanings; defined terms control even if ordinary speech differs.

B. Causes, property, persons, or situations the policy does not cover.

C. Crime coverage for dishonest acts by employees causing covered loss to the employer.

D. Pays benefits required by the workers compensation law of listed states; statutory benefits generally have no policy limit.

59. Which answer correctly applies the concept of Part Two - Employers Liability?

A. Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

B. Pays covered damages for employer liability not handled by workers compensation law, subject to stated limits and exclusions.

C. The insured's premium and truthful application plus the insurer's promise to pay covered claims.

D. One limit applies across multiple properties, locations, or classes of property.

60. Which statement best describes Prompt payment?

A. Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

B. Temporary income benefits replace part of lost wages during qualifying temporary disability.

C. Generally payment is due within 5 business days after the insurer notifies the claimant it will pay, subject to statutory exceptions.

sections.title: Master Flashcards
sections.html:
Master Flashcards

Cover the answer column and define the term aloud. Star any card that takes more than five seconds. Review starred cards morning and evening.

Term

Say this in plain English

Ch.

Risk

Uncertainty about loss. Insurance is designed mainly for pure risk, where loss or no loss - but not gain - is possible.

1

Peril

The immediate cause of loss, such as fire, wind, theft, collision, or lightning.

1

Hazard

A condition that increases the chance or severity of loss. Physical hazards are tangible; moral hazards involve dishonesty; morale hazards involve carelessness.

1

Exposure

A person, property, activity, or condition subject to possible loss.

1

Direct loss

Immediate physical damage caused by a covered peril, such as hail damaging a roof.

1

Indirect loss

A consequence of direct loss, such as lost rent while a damaged house is repaired.

1

Proximate cause

The dominant, efficient cause that sets an unbroken chain of events in motion.

1

Indemnity

Restoring the insured approximately to the financial position held before the loss - not allowing profit from insurance.

1

Insurable interest

A lawful financial relationship in which the insured would suffer loss if the property is damaged or the liability occurs.

1

Subrogation

After paying a covered loss, the insurer acquires the insured's right to recover from a responsible third party.

1

Salvage

The insurer's right to damaged property or its residual value after paying a total loss.

1

Law of large numbers

As the number of similar independent exposure units grows, actual loss experience becomes more predictable.

1

Declarations

The customized facts: named insured, policy period, locations, limits, deductibles, forms, and premium.

2

Insuring agreement

The insurer's basic promise to pay or perform, subject to the rest of the policy.

2

Definitions

Words given special policy meanings; defined terms control even if ordinary speech differs.

2

Exclusions

Causes, property, persons, or situations the policy does not cover.

2

Conditions

Rules and duties governing coverage, such as prompt notice, cooperation, proof of loss, and protecting property.

2

Endorsement

A written form that adds, deletes, or changes policy provisions and generally controls over conflicting base-form language.

2

Binder

Temporary evidence of insurance until the policy is issued or the binder expires.

2

Consideration

The insured's premium and truthful application plus the insurer's promise to pay covered claims.

2

Adhesion

The insurer drafts the contract; genuine ambiguity is generally construed against the drafter.

2

Aleatory

The values exchanged may be unequal and depend on an uncertain event.

2

Unilateral

Only the insurer makes a legally enforceable promise to pay if conditions are met.

2

Conditional

The insurer's obligation depends on the insured satisfying policy duties and conditions.

2

Representation

A statement believed true to the best of the applicant's knowledge; a material false statement can affect coverage.

2

Warranty

A statement or promise guaranteed to be true; it is stronger than a representation.

2

Concealment

Intentional failure to disclose a material fact.

2

Waiver and estoppel

Waiver is voluntary surrender of a known right; estoppel prevents a party from asserting a right after conduct caused reasonable detrimental reliance.

2

Named-peril coverage

Covers only causes of loss listed in the policy; the insured generally must show a listed peril caused the loss.

3

Open-peril coverage

Covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited; exclusions become especially important.

3

Actual cash value

Common exam formula: replacement cost minus depreciation.

3

Replacement cost

Cost to repair or replace with property of like kind and quality without deduction for depreciation, subject to policy rules.

3

Market value

Price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller; land and location affect it.

3

Agreed value

The insured and insurer agree in advance on the value; a related endorsement may suspend coinsurance.

3

Stated value

A listed value that may still be subject to policy settlement terms; it is not automatically a guaranteed payout.

3

Coinsurance

Requires insurance to a specified percentage of value. Partial-loss payment is generally Did carry / Should have carried x Loss, minus deductible.

3

Specific insurance

One limit applies to one described property or location.

3

Blanket insurance

One limit applies across multiple properties, locations, or classes of property.

3

Appraisal

Resolves disputes about the amount of loss, not whether coverage exists.

3

Vacancy vs. unoccupancy

Vacant generally means substantially empty of people and contents needed for use; unoccupied means furnished but no one is present.

3

HO-2 Broad

Named-peril coverage for dwelling, other structures, and personal property.

4

HO-3 Special

Open-peril coverage on dwelling and other structures; named-peril coverage on personal property. The most common owner-occupied form.

4

HO-4 Contents Broad

Renters coverage; primarily personal property, loss of use, liability, and medical payments, not the building.

4

HO-5 Comprehensive

Open-peril coverage on dwelling, other structures, and personal property, subject to exclusions.

4

HO-6 Unit-Owners

Condominium unit-owner coverage for personal property, certain building items, loss assessments, liability, and additional living expense.

4

HO-8 Modified Coverage

Designed for older homes when replacement cost may greatly exceed market value; uses more limited perils and modified settlement.

4

DP-1 Basic

Basic named perils, commonly fire, lightning, and internal explosion; extended coverage and vandalism may be added.

4

DP-2 Broad

Broader named-peril protection and typically replacement-cost settlement on covered buildings when requirements are met.

4

DP-3 Special

Open-peril building coverage with named-peril personal-property coverage.

4

Coverage A-D

A dwelling, B other structures, C personal property, D loss of use.

4

Coverage E-F

E personal liability; F medical payments to others, generally without requiring proof of negligence.

4

Personal articles floater

Scheduled inland-marine coverage for high-value movable property, usually broader than homeowners special limits.

4

Liability coverage

Pays damages for bodily injury or property damage for which an insured becomes legally responsible, plus defense and supplementary payments.

5

Medical payments

Pays reasonable medical and funeral expenses for covered persons, generally without regard to fault and subject to time/limit provisions.

5

PIP

Broader no-fault protection than medical payments because it can include lost income and essential services in addition to medical expenses.

5

UM/UIM

Protects insureds when an at-fault driver has no insurance, insufficient limits, or in covered hit-and-run situations.

5

Collision

Upset of the covered auto or impact with another vehicle or object.

5

Other than collision

Examples include theft, fire, vandalism, glass breakage, flood, hail, falling objects, and contact with a bird or animal.

5

Temporary substitute

A non-owned auto temporarily used because a covered auto is out of normal use due to breakdown, repair, servicing, loss, or destruction.

5

Newly acquired auto

An auto the named insured becomes owner of during the policy period, subject to policy notice and coverage rules.

5

Non-owned auto

A vehicle not owned by or furnished/available for the regular use of the named insured or family member.

5

Split limits

Separate per-person bodily injury, per-accident bodily injury, and per-accident property damage limits.

5

Combined single limit

One liability limit applies to bodily injury and property damage together per accident.

5

Transportation expense

Limited reimbursement for temporary transportation after a covered physical-damage loss, subject to form triggers and limits.

5

CPP

A modular commercial package built from common declarations/conditions plus selected coverage parts; it is not itself one coverage grant.

6

Commercial property form

Can cover buildings, business personal property, and personal property of others within described rules and limits.

6

Basic/Broad/Special causes of loss

Basic and Broad list named causes; Special covers direct physical loss unless excluded or limited.

6

Business income

Covers qualifying loss of net income plus continuing normal operating expenses during the period of restoration after covered direct damage.

6

Extra expense

Covers necessary extra costs to avoid or minimize suspension and continue operations after covered damage.

6

Period of restoration

Begins after the covered direct loss subject to the form and ends when property should be repaired/rebuilt or operations resume at a new location, as defined.

6

BOP

A packaged policy for eligible small-to-medium businesses combining property and liability, with standardized coverage and eligibility rules.

6

Builders risk

Covers buildings or structures during construction and specified materials, subject to form and project status.

6

Inland marine

Covers movable property, property in transit, instrumentalities of transportation/communication, and certain unique property exposures.

6

Equipment breakdown

Addresses accidental mechanical/electrical breakdown and related property/business-income consequences that ordinary property forms may exclude.

6

Cyber first-party

Can cover the insured's own response, restoration, business interruption, notification, and extortion expenses, depending on form.

6

NFIP

Federal flood program offering separate building and contents coverage. Standard property and homeowners policies generally exclude flood.

6

CGL Coverage A

Bodily injury and property damage liability caused by an occurrence, subject to territory, period, exclusions, and limits.

7

CGL Coverage B

Personal and advertising injury offenses, such as certain false arrest, libel, slander, and advertising wrongs, subject to exclusions.

7

CGL Coverage C

Limited medical payments for qualifying injuries, generally without proof of negligence.

7

Premises and operations

Liability arising from the insured's premises or ongoing operations.

7

Products-completed operations

Liability after a product leaves the insured's control or work is completed away from the insured's premises.

7

Occurrence form

Generally triggered by covered injury or damage occurring during the policy period, even if the claim is made later.

7

Claims-made form

Generally requires the claim to be first made during the policy period or reporting period and after any applicable retroactive date.

7

Retroactive date

Cuts off coverage for injury-causing acts occurring before the stated date under a claims-made form.

7

Extended reporting period

Additional time to report claims after claims-made coverage ends; it does not extend the policy period or cover new acts.

7

Aggregate limit

The most the policy pays for specified categories of covered loss during the policy period.

7

Umbrella

Provides higher limits and may cover some claims not covered by underlying insurance, subject to retention and terms.

7

Excess liability

Adds limits above underlying coverage and generally follows the underlying scope more closely.

7

Professional liability

Covers liability arising from specialized professional services; examples include malpractice and errors and omissions.

7

EPLI

Targets employment-related claims such as wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

7

Symbol 1 - Any auto

Broad liability designation that can include owned, hired, and non-owned autos when shown.

8

Symbol 2 - Owned autos only

Covers autos the insured owns, subject to the coverage shown.

8

Symbol 7 - Specifically described autos

Covers only autos scheduled in the policy for the indicated coverage.

8

Symbol 8 - Hired autos

Autos the insured leases, hires, rents, or borrows, subject to definition and exceptions.

8

Symbol 9 - Non-owned autos

Autos not owned, leased, hired, rented, or borrowed by the business but used in its business, often employee-owned vehicles.

8

Garagekeepers

Covers customers' autos in the insured's care, custody, or control for servicing, repair, parking, or similar operations.

8

Employee dishonesty

Crime coverage for dishonest acts by employees causing covered loss to the employer.

8

Theft

Broad unlawful taking of property.

8

Burglary

Taking property from inside premises by a person making felonious entry or exit, typically with visible signs as defined.

8

Robbery

Taking property from a person by force, threat, or violence.

8

Forgery and alteration

Crime coverage for specified loss involving forged or altered checks, drafts, and similar instruments.

8

Surety bond

Three parties: principal promises performance, obligee receives the promise, and surety guarantees it. The surety expects reimbursement from the principal.

8

Fidelity bond

Protects an employer or organization against employee dishonesty; it resembles insurance more than a performance guarantee.

8

Part One - Workers Compensation

Pays benefits required by the workers compensation law of listed states; statutory benefits generally have no policy limit.

9

Part Two - Employers Liability

Pays covered damages for employer liability not handled by workers compensation law, subject to stated limits and exclusions.

9

Part Three - Other States

Provides temporary protection when operations begin in listed other states, subject to policy conditions and monopolistic-state limitations.

9

Exclusive remedy

Workers compensation benefits generally replace an employee's tort suit against a covered employer for ordinary work injury, subject to exceptions.

9

Medical benefits

Reasonable and necessary care for a compensable work injury, as state law provides.

9

Income/disability benefits

Replace a portion of wages when a compensable injury reduces earning ability, subject to law.

9

Death and burial benefits

Statutory benefits for eligible beneficiaries and funeral costs after covered work-related death.

9

Occupational disease

Disease arising from employment conditions rather than an ordinary disease of life, subject to legal definitions.

9

Premium basis

Classification rate x payroll / 100, adjusted by experience modification and other rating elements; final premium is commonly audited.

9

Experience modification

Compares an employer's loss experience with expected experience; above 1.00 tends to increase premium and below 1.00 tends to decrease it.

9

Federal acts

Special laws such as FELA and the U.S. Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act may govern defined workers/exposures.

9

Duty

A legal obligation to act or refrain from acting with the required standard of care.

14

Breach

Failure to meet the required standard of care.

14

Causation

The breach must be both the actual and legally proximate cause of injury.

14

Damages

The claimant must suffer legally recognized harm.

14

Special compensatory damages

Measurable economic losses such as medical bills, lost wages, and repair costs.

14

General compensatory damages

Non-economic harm such as pain, suffering, mental anguish, or disfigurement.

14

Punitive damages

Designed to punish and deter especially wrongful conduct rather than compensate ordinary loss.

14

Strict liability

Liability without the ordinary need to prove negligence for defined activities or defective products; defenses and statutes still matter.

14

Absolute liability

An even stronger form of liability imposed by law for certain activities, with very limited defenses.

14

Vicarious liability

Liability imposed on one party for another's acts because of a legal relationship, such as an employer for an employee acting in scope.

14

Supplementary payments

Amounts such as defense costs, certain bonds, interest, or expenses paid in addition to liability limits when the policy so provides.

14

Contribution

Allocation among insurers or responsible parties that share the same loss.

14

ACV formula

Replacement cost - depreciation = actual cash value.

15

Coinsurance formula

Amount carried / amount required x covered loss - deductible, never exceeding applicable limit or loss.

15

Amount required

Property value x coinsurance percentage.

15

Split-limit sequence

Apply the per-person bodily injury cap, then the per-accident bodily injury cap, then the separate property damage cap.

15

Workers comp manual premium

Payroll / 100 x classification rate, then apply experience and other rating modifications.

15

Loss ratio

Incurred losses divided by earned premium; useful as an underwriting/performance concept.

15

Four-pass exam method

Answer confident items; solve short scenarios; perform calculations; return to flagged items with remaining time.

15

Qualifiers

Words such as EXCEPT, NOT, BEST, FIRST, PRIMARY, and MOST LIKELY change the task and should be marked mentally.

15

Commissioner of Insurance

Administers and enforces Texas insurance law, examines and investigates regulated persons, conducts hearings, issues orders, and can impose authorized sanctions.

10

Certificate of authority

State authorization for an insurer to transact specified insurance business in Texas.

10

Domestic insurer

Organized under Texas law.

10

Foreign insurer

Organized under another U.S. state or jurisdiction.

10

Alien insurer

Organized under the laws of another country.

10

Admitted/authorized insurer

Holds Texas authority for the business being transacted; nonadmitted insurers may be used only through lawful mechanisms such as surplus lines.

10

Stock insurer

Owned by stockholders.

10

Mutual insurer

Owned by policyholders.

10

Appointment

An insurer's authorization for an agent to act on its behalf, subject to Texas filing and termination rules.

10

General Lines P&C scope

Allows sale of home, auto, commercial, liability, and other property/casualty lines within license authority.

10

Continuing education

Current Texas general lines requirement: 24 hours each two-year license period, including 3 hours of ethics.

10

Misrepresentation

False or misleading statements about policy terms, benefits, dividends, financial condition, or another material insurance matter.

10

Rebating

Offering an inducement not stated in the contract to influence purchase, when prohibited by law.

10

Defamation

False, maliciously critical, or derogatory statements intended to injure an insurer's or person's reputation.

10

Unfair claims practice

Conduct such as misrepresenting coverage, failing to investigate reasonably, or not attempting prompt fair settlement when liability is reasonably clear.

10

Texas FAIR Plan

Residential property insurer of last resort offering basic coverage when eligible applicants cannot obtain coverage in the voluntary admitted market; TDI guidance says at least two companies must decline.

11

TWIA

Insurer of last resort for windstorm and hail in designated catastrophe areas along the Texas coast, subject to eligibility and building-code compliance requirements.

11

WPI-8 certificate

Evidence of compliance that is commonly proof of eligibility for TWIA wind/hail coverage for applicable structures.

11

Surplus lines

Coverage placed with eligible nonadmitted insurers for qualifying risks that cannot be placed in the admitted market, through properly licensed surplus lines channels.

11

Guaranty association

Pays eligible covered claims when a member insurer becomes insolvent, subject to statutory exclusions and limits. Texas consumer guidance notes no dollar limit for workers compensation benefits.

11

Prompt acknowledgement

Generally within 15 calendar days after notice of a first-party claim, the insurer acknowledges, begins investigation, and requests needed items.

11

Prompt decision

Generally within 15 business days after receiving required items, the insurer accepts or rejects; it may extend up to 45 days with notice and reason.

11

Prompt payment

Generally payment is due within 5 business days after the insurer notifies the claimant it will pay, subject to statutory exceptions.

11

Home cancellation

Current TDI consumer guidance states the company must give 10 days' notice before cancellation, subject to the policy and law.

11

Home nonrenewal

Current TDI guidance generally requires 60 days' notice for policies bought or renewed in 2024 or later; older-transition rules may differ.

11

Liquidated demand

Texas-specific statutory concept referenced in the exam outline for certain fire-loss claims; learn the outline reference, TIC Section 862.053, and read the question's facts carefully.

11

30/60/25

$30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 property damage per accident - Texas minimum financial responsibility limits.

12

Texas PIP

Included/offered in Texas auto policies at a statutory minimum of $2,500 unless the named insured rejects it in writing; pays covered medical expenses plus qualifying lost income/essential services.

12

Texas UM/UIM

Insurers must offer it; the named insured may reject it in writing. It may cover bodily injury, property damage, and qualifying hit-and-run loss subject to form and deductibles.

12

Proof of financial responsibility

A driver must be able to show compliance through an allowed method, most commonly liability insurance meeting minimum limits.

12

TAIPA

Texas Automobile Insurance Plan Association makes required auto liability coverage available to eligible applicants unable to obtain it through the voluntary market.

12

Auto cancellation

Current TDI guidance states a company must give 10 days' notice before it cancels a personal auto policy, subject to law and policy rules.

12

Auto nonrenewal

Current TDI guidance requires at least 60 days' notice of nonrenewal.

12

Unearned premium

The portion paid for coverage after cancellation; current TDI guidance says it must be refunded within 15 days after cancellation.

12

Rideshare/TNC exposure

Coverage needs change when the app is off, on and waiting, and carrying or traveling to a passenger. Personal policies may exclude commercial/livery activity.

12

Subscriber

An employer providing Texas workers compensation through an authorized carrier, certified self-insurance, or another lawful method.

13

Nonsubscriber

An employer that does not provide Texas statutory workers compensation and must meet notice/reporting requirements.

13

Texas private employer rule

Most private employers may choose whether to carry workers compensation; private employers on government contracts may be required to cover project workers.

13

Governmental entities

Texas public schools, utilities, cities, and counties must provide workers compensation coverage.

13

Subscriber protection

A subscriber is protected from most employee negligence suits; a fatal injury caused by employer gross negligence is an important exception.

13

Nonsubscriber defenses

When sued, a nonsubscriber generally loses traditional defenses including employee contributory negligence, fellow-servant negligence, and assumption of risk.

13

TIBs

Temporary income benefits replace part of lost wages during qualifying temporary disability.

13

IIBs

Impairment income benefits are tied to a permanent impairment rating after maximum medical improvement.

13

SIBs

Supplemental income benefits may follow IIBs for qualifying serious impairment and reduced earnings, subject to requirements.

13

LIBs

Lifetime income benefits apply to specifically defined catastrophic injuries.

13

Medical, death, burial

Other major statutory benefit categories for compensable injury or death.

13

sections.title: Exam-Day Checklist
sections.html:
Exam-Day Checklist

Verify the exact test-center address and arrive 30 minutes early.

Bring two current signature IDs. Primary ID must be government-issued, photo-bearing, signed, unexpired, and in English. Registration name must match exactly.

Complete the computer tutorial; tutorial time does not reduce exam time.

On the first pass, answer sure questions and flag slow ones. Never leave an answer blank.

Mark qualifiers: NOT, EXCEPT, BEST, FIRST, PRIMARY, and MOST LIKELY.

For coverage questions use: person/property -> cause of loss -> coverage grant -> exclusion -> condition -> limit/deductible.

For Texas questions, recall written rejections, exact notices, residual-market purpose, and consumer-protection duties.

If two choices seem plausible, choose the one that answers the exact coverage or legal issue asked - not a broader fact that is merely true.

Final mindset You do not need perfection. You need disciplined recognition, careful reading, and a safe margin above the passing standard.
